title: Electrochemistry Cell with Voltage Control
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D electrochemistry cell (galvanic/electrolytic) using Three.js. The scene must be fully self-contained with no external dependencies except Three.js from CDN.

## Scene Setup
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 5, 12), looking at origin. Add OrbitControls for rotation/zoom.
- Lighting: One directional light from (5, 10, 5) intensity 1.0, one ambient light intensity 0.4.
- Background: dark gradient (0x1a1a2e).

## 3D Cell Construction
- A transparent rectangular glass beaker (BoxGeometry with transparent material, opacity 0.25, color 0x88ccff) centered at origin, size roughly (6, 4, 3).
- A vertical partition wall inside the beaker (thin box, semi-transparent, 0xcccccc) dividing it into left and right half-cells. The partition represents a salt bridge / porous membrane.
- Left electrode (anode): A cylinder (radius 0.3, height 3) colored copper-brown (0xb87333) positioned in the left half-cell. Label it 'Cu' using a sprite or DOM overlay.
- Right electrode (cathode): A cylinder (radius 0.3, height 3) colored silver-gray (0xc0c0c0) positioned in the right half-cell. Label it 'Zn' using a sprite or DOM overlay.
- Electrolyte: Two semi-transparent box volumes filling each half-cell to a certain level. Left electrolyte is blue-tinted (CuSO4), right is colorless/light gray (ZnSO4).
- Wire: A curved line (THREE.CatmullRomCurve3) connecting the tops of both electrodes above the beaker, colored 0xffcc00 (gold wire).

## Particle System (Ion Flow)
- Create particle systems representing ion movement in each half-cell.
- Cu2+ ions (small blue spheres, 8-12 particles) in the left half-cell.
- Zn2+ ions (small gray spheres, 8-12 particles) in the right half-cell.
- Electron particles (tiny yellow spheres, 6-10) flowing along the wire from anode to cathode.
- Particle speed and direction depend on the applied voltage and cell mode.

## Voltage Control
- A DOM slider input (range: -3.0V to +3.0V, step 0.1, default 0.0V) at the bottom of the screen.
- A DOM label showing the current voltage value.
- The standard cell potential E°cell = +1.10V (Cu/Zn cell).
- When voltage slider is at 0V: the cell operates as a galvanic cell at its natural E°cell. Electrons flow from Zn (anode, oxidation) to Cu (cathode, reduction). Zn electrode slowly shrinks, Cu electrode slowly grows.
- When external voltage is applied (slider moved):
  - If appliedVoltage < E°cell (e.g., 0 to +1.09V): galvanic mode continues, electron flow rate = (E°cell - appliedVoltage) * baseRate.
  - If appliedVoltage >= E°cell: electrolytic mode. Electron flow reverses direction. Cu dissolves, Zn plates. Flow rate = (appliedVoltage - E°cell) * baseRate.
  - Negative voltage increases galvanic driving force: flow rate = (E°cell + |appliedVoltage|) * baseRate.

## Mode Indicator
- A DOM element showing current mode: 'GALVANIC' (green text) or 'ELECTROLYTIC' (red text).
- The mode switches based on the voltage threshold described above.

## Electrode Mass Simulation
- Track electrode masses: Cu starts at 100 units, Zn starts at 100 units.
- In galvanic mode: Zn mass decreases, Cu mass increases over time proportional to flow rate.
- In electrolytic mode: Cu mass decreases, Zn mass increases.
- Electrode cylinder scaleY changes proportionally to mass (mass/100 * originalScale).
- Mass is clamped to [10, 200] range. If either electrode hits 10, flow stops (depleted state).
- Display both masses in a DOM HUD panel (top-right corner).

## Buttons
- 'Reset' button: resets voltage to 0, masses to 100, restores electrode sizes.
- 'Pause/Resume' button: toggles simulation pause state.
- 'Boost' button: temporarily doubles the flow rate for 3 seconds, then returns to normal.

## Keyboard Controls
- Arrow Up/Down: increase/decrease voltage by 0.1V.
- Space: toggle pause.
- 'R' key: reset.
- 'B' key: activate boost.

## Conservation Law
- Total mass (Cu mass + Zn mass) must remain constant at 200 units at all times (mass transferred from one electrode to the other).

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with these fields updated every frame:
- voltage: current voltage (number)
- mode: 'galvanic' or 'electrolytic' (string)
- cuMass: copper electrode mass (number)
- znMass: zinc electrode mass (number)
- totalMass: cuMass + znMass (should always be 200)
- flowRate: current electron flow rate (number, >= 0)
- electronCount: number of electron particles currently active (number)
- cuIonCount: number of Cu2+ ion particles (number)
- znIonCount: number of Zn2+ ion particles (number)
- isPaused: boolean
- isBoosted: boolean
- boostTimeRemaining: number (seconds remaining on boost, 0 if not boosted)
- isDepleted: boolean (true if any electrode mass <= 10)
- cuElectrodeScaleY: current Y scale of Cu electrode (number)
- znElectrodeScaleY: current Y scale of Zn electrode (number)
- elapsedTime: total simulation time in seconds (number, paused time excluded)
- particleSpeedMultiplier: 1.0 normally, 2.0 when boosted
physics_constraints: Conservation of total electrode mass: cuMass + znMass = 200 at all times. Electrode mass clamped to [10, 200]. Flow rate must be non-negative. Galvanic/electrolytic mode threshold at appliedVoltage = E°cell = 1.10V. Electron flow direction reverses at mode switch. Flow stops when either electrode is depleted (mass <= 10). Nernst-like voltage-rate relationship: rate proportional to |net driving voltage|.
